description: Snowflake-Scripting loop-control and cursor-scope behaviour, two cases of which were defective. CONTINUE must skip only the rest of the CURRENT ITERATION and its signal must not leak PAST the loop and abort the enclosing block - the regression is that the flag used to abort the block, so the RETURN after the loop never ran and the block produced no row at all - verified across WHILE, FOR-range and REPEAT. RETURN inside a loop exits the loop and the block immediately; a FOR counter carries no declared type, so RETURNing it directly makes the result TEXT. A procedural cursor is scoped to its EXECUTION, so a cursor name can be re-declared by a later top-level statement on the same session without a spurious 'Cursor already declared' - asserted by running the same block twice, for the FOR form and for OPEN / FETCH / CLOSE. And a DECLAREd exception is caught by its NAMED handler while WHEN OTHER catches a runtime error. Converted 1:1 from scripting/LoopContinueAndCursorScopeTest (now retired); its REPEAT test carried an Assumptions.assumeFalse(isLiveSnowflake()) because Snowflake aborts that exact block with its own internal error 300010, reproduced under two different incident numbers - so it is their defect, not a divergence - and that becomes skip snowflake with the reason kept.

steps.sql: DECLARE i INTEGER DEFAULT 0; s INTEGER DEFAULT 0; BEGIN WHILE (i < 5) DO i := i + 1; IF (MOD(i,2) = 1) THEN CONTINUE; END IF; s := s + i; END WHILE; RETURN s; END
DECLARE s INTEGER DEFAULT 0; BEGIN FOR i IN 1 TO 5 DO IF (MOD(i,2) = 1) THEN CONTINUE; END IF; s := s + i; END FOR; RETURN s; END

skip.reason: Snowflake aborts this exact block with its own internal error (Processing aborted due to error 300010, with an incident number), reproduced on two separate runs under different incident numbers, so it is their defect rather than a divergence; frostlake's answer stays asserted on the embedded path

steps.sql: DECLARE i INTEGER DEFAULT 0; s INTEGER DEFAULT 0; BEGIN REPEAT i := i + 1; IF (MOD(i,2) = 1) THEN CONTINUE; END IF; s := s + i; UNTIL (i >= 5) END REPEAT; RETURN s; END
DECLARE i INTEGER DEFAULT 0; BEGIN WHILE (i < 10) DO i := i + 1; IF (i = 3) THEN RETURN i; END IF; END WHILE; RETURN -1; END
BEGIN FOR i IN 1 TO 10 DO IF (i = 4) THEN RETURN i; END IF; END FOR; RETURN -1; END
DECLARE s INTEGER DEFAULT 0; c CURSOR FOR SELECT n FROM cscope; BEGIN FOR r IN c DO s := s + r.n; END FOR; RETURN s; END
DECLARE s INTEGER DEFAULT 0; c CURSOR FOR SELECT n FROM cscope; BEGIN FOR r IN c DO s := s + r.n; END FOR; RETURN s; END
DECLARE v INTEGER; c CURSOR FOR SELECT n FROM cvals ORDER BY n; BEGIN OPEN c; FETCH c INTO v; CLOSE c; RETURN v; END
DECLARE v INTEGER; c CURSOR FOR SELECT n FROM cvals ORDER BY n; BEGIN OPEN c; FETCH c INTO v; CLOSE c; RETURN v; END
DECLARE e EXCEPTION (-20001, 'boom'); BEGIN RAISE e; EXCEPTION WHEN e THEN RETURN 'caught'; END
BEGIN RETURN 1 / 0; EXCEPTION WHEN OTHER THEN RETURN 'handled'; END
